transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-15
Time: 16:00 - 16:52 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Martins (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion - Head of Platform), Tom Becker (Orion - Lead Eng), Aisha Khan (Orion - Security)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
- Initial integration discovery for Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
- Key integration topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting & quotas, observability hooks and tracing.
- Security questions: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML.
- Next steps: send security docs, SDK examples, run benchmark, schedule technical deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick audio check?
[00:04] Priya Nair: Yeah audible, thanks.
[00:06] Samantha Lee: Great. I'm Sam, AE on the account, and Diego is our SE, he will handle the deep technical stuff. Could we do quick intros?
[00:15] Priya Nair: Sure, I'm Priya, head of platform at Orion. We're evaluating options for powering search and summarization features across our product.
[00:22] Tom Becker: Tom, lead engineer, I'll be owning the integration.
[00:25] Aisha Khan: Aisha from security, I'll be looking at network and key mgmt.
[00:29] Diego Martins: Hi all, Diego, happy to dive into SDKs and performance.

[00:35] Samantha Lee: Cool, Priya can you give a bit of context on current stack and what you're trying to achieve?
[00:40] Priya Nair: Yeah so we run primarily on GCP, k8s, microservices. We already have some OpenAI usage for front-end features but costs are getting kinda high. We're evaluating Redwood for predictable cost and the option to run private — like VPC or on-prem for certain regulated customers. Main goals: sub-300ms median latency for short prompt completions, decent cost per 1k tokens, and strong auditability.
[01:05] Tom Becker: We also use LangChain internally for orchestration of chains and retrieval. We want to know how Redwood integrates — direct SDK, LangChain connectors, or if we need a custom gateway.
[01:16] Samantha Lee: Great. Diego — do you want to cover integration touchpoints?
[01:19] Diego Martins: Yeah for sure. So Redwood provides REST and SDKs — Node, Python, Go — and we have example LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors.
[01:30] Diego Martins: The Node SDK is straightforward: api key or mTLS for private, and you can swap endpoints between hosted and dedicated. For LangChain, we have a small adapter that implements the LLMMeta interface — folks commonly drop it into chains. The LlamaIndex bits are similar, usually just change the client init.
[01:44] Tom Becker: Is that adapter open source or do we get snippets?
[01:48] Diego Martins: We can share snippets; it's on our docs repo, and we also have a sample repo that shows a proxy/gateway pattern that Orion might like — a lightweight gateway that adds request-level routing, auth, per-tenant rate limits.
[01:58] Priya Nair: When you say gateway, do you mean we need an extra proxy in front of Redwood? We'd prefer minimizing infra changes.
[02:04] Diego Martins: It's optional. For hosted customers it's optional; you can call Redwood directly from your services with api keys scoped to teams. For Dedicated/Private some customers prefer a local gateway to centralize quotas and observability, especially if they want to add additional request enrichment or funneling. The sample gateway is just an nginx/envoy + small auth service example.
[02:24] Aisha Khan: From security perspective, if we go Private, we need KMS integration and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. How does Redwood support that?
[02:31] Samantha Lee: Good question. We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we can enable envelope encryption with our key rotation options. Audit logs are available via our console and can be exported to S3 or a push to a logging endpoint for SIEM. I'll share the exact docs after the call.
[02:48] Aisha Khan: Also SSO — SAML? RBAC?
[02:51] Diego Martins: Yes SAML/SSO for the console, and we support RBAC at token and team level. For API-level RBAC we usually recommend issuing per-service API tokens and scoping them with projects/roles.
[03:05] Tom Becker: Back to integration — rate limits and quotas: we need per-tenant quotas and burst handling. How fine-grained are your quotas?
[03:12] Diego Martins: Quotas can be configured per-key, per-project, and you can apply per-tenant policies. For Dedicated we have more advanced token bucket controls and burst windows. There's also a graceful degradation policy where requests can fall back to a cheaper model variant if capacity is constrained.
[03:28] Priya Nair: Can we set soft vs hard limits? Like soft alert at 80% and hard at 100%?
[03:33] Diego Martins: Yep, thresholds, alerts, and webhook hooks are available — we can trigger alerts to PagerDuty or a webhook for your infra.
[03:40] Priya Nair: Observability hooks — we use OpenTelemetry across our services. Does Redwood emit traces or do we need to instrument the gateway?
[03:47] Diego Martins: Redwood can emit request-level metrics to Prometheus for Dedicated and Private. For tracing, we support OpenTelemetry span injection for responses and you can pass in trace headers from your services. If you use a gateway, it's often easiest to capture full spans there.
[04:00] Tom Becker: Nice. For the LangChain usage, latency is key — we do retrieval-augmented generation with 2-3 synchronous calls per user request. If median is 300ms per call that's 600-900ms total — tight. Any tuning guidance?
[04:13] Diego Martins: We generally recommend three levers: model choice (smaller models for short completions), batching where possible, and prefix/KV caching. Redwood's serving runtime supports KV cache reuse between calls when you keep sessions. Also for dedicated pools you can request low-latency GPUs and we tune kernel selection to favor latency over throughput.
[04:32] Samantha Lee: To add, our Optimize tool will analyze your prompt set and recommend quantization/profile and batching settings to hit latency vs cost targets. We can run that on your sample prompts.
[04:41] Priya Nair: Is the Optimize tool available on Private too?
[04:44] Diego Martins: Yes, for Private we ship a version that integrates with the local console; for on-prem we provide an opt-in agent that uploads anonymized perf stats if you want Redwood Advice.
[04:55] Aisha Khan: On data residency — some customers require EU-only processing. How flexible are regions for Hosted?
[04:59] Samantha Lee: Hosted API supports region pinning — you can opt to keep data in specific cloud regions. For Dedicated, capacity is region-specific and we can do contracts to pin to eu-west or us-east. Private gives you full control since it's your VPC or on-prem.
[05:12] Tom Becker: A note on SDKs — we saw in the docs that there is a streaming API. Does streaming preserve trace information and is it compatible with LangChain streaming interfaces?
[05:21] Diego Martins: Yes streaming uses server-sent events and preserves headers including trace IDs. Our LangChain adapter plugs into the streaming hooks so you can stream tokens back into your chain orchestration. There are some quirks around reconnects where the SDK handles rehydration but you should test with your UI.
[05:36] Priya Nair: About quota enforcement and billing — we need visibility of cost per route and per-team. Does your console have that granularity?
[05:43] Samantha Lee: Console shows token-level cost breakdown by route, model, and API key. For Dedicated we can also ship more detailed billing exports to S3 or to your billing system.
[05:51] Aisha Khan: For Private deployments we want to manage keys with our HashiCorp vault. Integrations?
[05:55] Diego Martins: We support HashiCorp Vault via our connector; it's a supported pattern. For on-prem we can also support HSM via PKCS#11 if needed.
[06:05] Tom Becker: Performance testing — we'd like to run a 48-hour POC to validate latency and cost. What's a typical POC flow?
[06:12] Samantha Lee: Usually we do a short discovery (this call), then an SE-run benchmark: you share sample prompts and QPS, we run against Hosted first and then optionally Dedicated. We'll supply a script and you'll run it from your environment or we can run it from Redwood side with your data. Diego?
[06:26] Diego Martins: We'll put together a benchmark plan: synthetic & representative prompts, concurrency targets, and we'll measure p50/p95; also track cost per 1k tokens.
[06:34] Priya Nair: For the benchmark will you include the gateway overhead if we use that pattern?
[06:38] Diego Martins: Yes we can include a gateway in the loop; we have a sample envoy config used in our docs.
[06:44] Tom Becker: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex connectors — we've seen index mismatch issues and token inflation.
[06:49] Diego Martins: Common gotchas: embedding dimension mismatch if you plug a different embedder, and chunk sizes causing more tokens. We recommend validating embeddings and using the Redwood embed API which is tuned for a few common models.
[06:59] Priya Nair: On the topic of embeddings — are they billed differently? And how do you handle retention?
[07:04] Samantha Lee: Embeddings are billed per-unit. Retention defaults to 30 days for Hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies or disable retention entirely; for Private it's customer-controlled.
[07:15] Aisha Khan: We need an audit trail for every API call with requester id, request payload hash, model used, and response hash. Can Redwood provide that?
[07:23] Diego Martins: Yes we can provide detailed audit logs including request metadata, tokens used, model id. For Hosted, logs are available in the console and exportable. For Dedicated/Private logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint or stored in your S3. Response hashing is something we can include as part of the POC if you want it baked into the audit pipeline.
[07:39] Priya Nair: Ok great. A couple quick clarifications: 1) If we start on Hosted and move to Dedicated later, how seamless is model pinning and rollout?
[07:48] Samantha Lee: It's designed to be seamless — same API surface. You can pin model versions per route and rollout with canaries/A-B inside the Console.
[07:56] Tom Becker: 2) Rate limiting per-tenant during spikes — what's the recommendation for client retries?
[08:01] Diego Martins: Exponential backoff with jitter is recommended. For spikes we recommend a token-bucket at gateway layer to smooth bursts and queue/async for non-interactive calls.
[08:10] Priya Nair: 3) Open source connectors — where are they hosted?
[08:13] Diego Martins: On our GitHub org; I'll share links. They include basic LangChain, LlamaIndex, and a sample envoy gateway.
[08:19] Samantha Lee: Alright let's recap. Next steps: Sam will send security docs + pricing. Diego will share SDK examples and the sample gateway repo and will run a benchmark plan once Priya shares prompt set. Aisha will share security questionnaire details and KMS constraints. We'll aim to follow up with a technical deep-dive the week of 4/26. Anything else?
[08:39] Priya Nair: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[08:42] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[08:43] Aisha Khan: Thanks.
